definitions.explanation: Food preserved in sealed metal containers.
Colloquially, being confined to a room working intensively without leaving.

examples.japanese: {災害|さいがい}{用|よう}に{缶詰|かんづめ}を{備蓄|びちく}している。
examples.english: I stock canned food for emergencies.

examples.japanese: ツナの{缶詰|かんづめ}を{開|あ}けた。
examples.english: I opened a can of tuna.

examples.japanese: {締|し}め{切|き}り{前|まえ}で{部屋|へや}に{缶詰|かんづめ}になっている。
examples.english: I'm holed up in my room because of the deadline.

notes:
{缶詰|かんづめ} refers to canned/tinned food, but also has a colloquial meaning.

Common expressions:
- {缶詰|かんづめ}を{開|あ}ける (to open a can)
- {缶詰|かんづめ}{食品|しょくひん} (canned food)
- {缶詰|かんづめ}になる/にする (to be holed up/to hole someone up)

Colloquial usage:
- {缶詰|かんづめ}{状態|じょうたい} (being confined, shut-in state)
- Often used for intensive work sessions before deadlines

The word combines {缶|かん} (can) + {詰|づ}め (packed/filled).
